# Photo Specifications

Schengen visa photos follow strict specifications (ICAO format with French adaptations). A non-compliant photo is **the most common reason for an appointment being delayed or rescheduled** — TLScontact may refuse to accept the application if the photo doesn't meet the spec.

> **Authoritative reference:** France-Visas and Schengen visa code Annex 11 / ICAO 9303 standards. The most recent guidance is on https://france-visas.gouv.fr/en/web/france-visas (search "photo specifications").

---

## Hard requirements

### Physical dimensions

| Specification | Value |
|---|---|
| **Photo size** | **35 mm wide × 45 mm tall** (3.5 × 4.5 cm) |
| Head height | 32–36 mm from chin to top of head |
| Head positioning | Centered horizontally, looking straight at camera |
| Eyes | Visible, open, looking at the camera |
| Eye line | Approximately 2/3 of the way up the photo |
| Background | **Plain, uniform, white** (not off-white, not grey, not blue) |
| Print quality | High resolution, no pixelation, sharp focus |

### Time + state

| Specification | Value |
|---|---|
| **Taken within** | Last **6 months** (more recent is better — appearance must match current you) |
| Quantity needed | **2 identical photos** per applicant |

### Appearance rules

| ✅ Must / ❌ Must not | Detail |
|---|---|
| ✅ **Neutral facial expression** | Closed mouth, no smile, lips relaxed |
| ✅ **Full face visible** | From hairline to chin |
| ✅ **Eyes open + clear** | Looking directly at camera |
| ✅ **Uniform white background** | Not patterned, not graded |
| ❌ **No glasses** | Take them off (even thin-frame, even non-tinted, even with no glare). Recent rule change — older photos with glasses may have been OK; today's standard is **no glasses** |
| ❌ **No hats / head coverings** | Exception: religious head coverings (hijab, turban) are allowed if the face from chin to forehead is fully visible |
| ❌ **No shadows** on the face or behind the head |
| ❌ **No red-eye / reflections** in eyes |
| ❌ **No filters / Photoshop** of any kind |
| ❌ **No earrings / large jewellery** that obscures the face |
| ✅ **Hair must not cover** eyes, eyebrows, or face edges |
| ✅ **Solid-coloured top** (any colour except white — needs contrast against the background) |

---

## Where to get photos

### Option 1 — Photo booth (cheapest, ~£5–8)

| Source | Notes |
|---|---|
| Photo-Me booths in supermarkets, post offices, train stations | Most UK booths now have a "Schengen" preset. Make sure you select it — not "UK Passport" (different size). |
| Photo-Me digital code service | Some booths print + give you a digital code to upload to France-Visas. ~£10. Useful for online upload. |

> **Tip:** Booth photos are often slightly grey-toned. If you have a choice, choose a booth with newer equipment.

### Option 2 — Professional photographer (£15–30)

Searches for "Schengen visa photo" or "French visa photo" in your area. Most high-street photography studios offer this. **Tell them explicitly "Schengen / France visa"** — UK passport photos are 45 × 35 mm but the French requirements differ in head-height + background tone.

### Option 3 — Online services (£10–20)

Various services let you upload a self-taken photo and they crop / format to spec, then mail printed photos. Examples (verify currency before relying):

| Service type | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| AI-validation services | Auto-checks compliance before printing | Quality depends on your phone camera + lighting |
| Print-and-mail services | Convenient, can do at home | 2–5 day delivery |
| Print-at-home options | Instant | Most home printers can't produce photo-quality at 35×45mm precisely |

### Option 4 — Take it yourself (NOT recommended for first-timers)

Possible with a good phone camera, a plain white sheet of paper behind you, and natural daylight. **Risky for first-time applicants** — TLScontact rejects ~10% of self-taken photos. If you're confident, follow:
- Phone on a tripod or stable surface at chin level
- Face the brightest natural-light window
- Plain white wall directly behind you (no posters, no curtains, no door frame visible)
- Use a photo-validation tool (free online) before printing
- Print at a photo-printing shop, not at home

---

## Pre-flight check (when photos arrive)

- [ ] Dimensions are 35 mm × 45 mm (measure with a ruler — many home prints come out slightly wrong)
- [ ] Background is **white**, not grey or beige
- [ ] **No glasses**
- [ ] Neutral expression, closed mouth, no smile
- [ ] Eyes open, looking at camera
- [ ] Head fills the right portion of the frame
- [ ] No shadows / no red-eye
- [ ] Photo is **less than 6 months old** (the photo, not the print)
- [ ] You have **2 identical copies** per applicant
- [ ] If France-Visas requested a digital photo: you have a JPEG ≤ 4 MB at the correct resolution

## Common pitfalls

| Pitfall | How to avoid |
|---|---|
| Took the photo wearing glasses | Re-take without glasses. Don't try to retouch — TLScontact will spot it. |
| Background is off-white / cream | Get a fresh photo with proper white background. Cream/beige is a common rejection. |
| Smiling slightly | Re-take with a fully neutral expression. Even a closed-mouth smile can be rejected. |
| Print came out slightly wrong size | Take a ruler to the photo. If it's not exactly 35 × 45 mm, get re-printed. |
| Photo is older than 6 months | Re-take. The "you must look like the photo" rule is real — they cross-check at biometrics. |
| Used same photo as for UK passport | UK passports are also 35 × 45 mm BUT the head-height + background-tone specs differ slightly. A UK photo is often **just barely** Schengen-compliant — review carefully. |
